title: Go / went / gone
subtitle: go to work, go swimming, be going to
summary: Use go to talk about moving from place to place, about future plans, and about activities like go swimming and go shopping.

lesson.heading: Go = move from one place to another
lesson.text: **Go** means to move from one place to another. We use it with places, with forms of transport and in questions about direction.

examples.text: I **go** to work by bike. My brother **goes** by car.
Shall we **go** to the swimming pool today?

lesson.heading: Go + prepositions
lesson.text: We often use **go** with a small word that shows the direction: **in(to)**, **out of**, **up** and **down**.

examples.text: Ethan **went into** his room and shut the door.
Yuko **went out of** the house and into the garden.
Jacob was tired. He **went up** the stairs slowly.
The phone was ringing. She **went down** the stairs quickly.

lesson.heading: Future plans: be going to
lesson.text: We often use **be going to** to talk about our plans for the future.

examples.text: Jan **is going to** study maths at university.
We're **going to** visit my aunt in New York soon.
I'm **going to** learn five new words every day.

lesson.heading: go + -ing for activities
rows: I hate going shopping on Saturdays.
I usually go swimming in the morning.
Do you like going sightseeing on holiday?
lesson.note: Never put to or for before the -ing word.

lesson.heading: Common mistakes
lesson.text: Three things to remember. We do not use *to* before an -ing activity, before **there**, **somewhere** or **anywhere**, or before **home**.

examples.wrong: go to swimming ... go for shopping

examples.text: I **go there** every week. I don't want to **go anywhere** else.
examples.wrong: go to there ... go to anywhere

lesson.text: Learn go home, go there and go swimming as whole phrases - then you will never add an extra to.

exercises.statement: I'm going to London by car tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Correct. We go to a city, and we travel by car.

exercises.statement: It's time to go at home now.
exercises.explanation: It's time to go home now. We never say go at home or go to home.

exercises.statement: Mum is going for shopping this afternoon.
exercises.explanation: Mum is going shopping this afternoon. There is no for before shopping.

exercises.prompt: I love Paris. Did you go ___ last year?
exercises.explanation: We say go there, not go to there.

exercises.prompt: We always go to the same cafe. Let's go ___ different today.
exercises.explanation: We say go somewhere, not go to somewhere.

exercises.prompt: She went out ___ the shop with her shopping bag.
exercises.explanation: We say go out of a place, not go out off.

exercises.prompt: Jo walked all the way to the top of the hill. Which sentence is correct?
options: Jo went up to the top of the hill.
Jo went down to the top of the hill.
Jo went out of the top of the hill.
Jo went into the top of the hill.
exercises.explanation: We go up to the top and down to the bottom.

exercises.prompt: We want to buy some new clothes this afternoon. What do we say?
exercises.explanation: Go + -ing for activities: go shopping, go swimming, go fishing.

exercises.prompt: Does each word come after go on its own, or after go to?
Victoria wrote her New Year resolutions. Match each plan with the right ending.

pairs.left: This year Victoria is going to stop
This year Victoria is going to pass
This year Victoria is going to learn
This year Victoria is going to watch
This year Victoria is going to keep

exercises.prompt: Victoria has a plan for this year. She ___ learn Spanish.
exercises.explanation: We use be going to for future plans.

exercises.prompt: Write Victoria's plan about her driving test.
exercises.answer: This year Victoria is going to pass her driving test.
exercises.explanation: be going to + verb talks about a plan.

exercises.statement: Would you like to go to home now?
exercises.explanation: Would you like to go home now? We never put to before home.
